title: Data senior domain data lineage governance
topic: Data senior domain data lineage governance
question: What is data lineage, and why does it become critical as an organization's data platform grows?
idealAnswer:
Data lineage tracks where a piece of data came from and every transformation it went through, from original source to final table or report, both column-level and table-level lineage are useful

As the number of pipelines and tables grows, it becomes hard for any one person to know how a given metric was actually computed, lineage makes that traceable instead of tribal knowledge

Lineage supports impact analysis, e.g. before changing or deprecating a source table, you can see every downstream table and dashboard that depends on it and would break

Lineage supports debugging, e.g. if a number looks wrong, you can trace backward through the transformation chain to find where the error was introduced

Lineage is also central to governance and compliance, e.g. tracing where personally identifiable information flows through the system, to ensure it's properly access-controlled or deleted on request

A strong answer mentions that lineage can be captured automatically, e.g. parsing SQL/query logs or instrumenting orchestration tools, versus manually documented, and that automatic capture scales much better and stays accurate as pipelines change
